question.text: A stock broking firm processes multiple cash transactions for a client during a month. The individual transactions are Rs 3 lakh, Rs 4 lakh, and Rs 5 lakh. Under the PMLA record maintenance requirements, for which of the following aggregate values must a Cash Transaction Report (CTR) be filed with FIU-IND?

answer.text: Rs 5 lakh, since only individual transactions above Rs 5 lakh need reporting
Rs 12 lakh, since the aggregate exceeds the Rs 10 lakh threshold requiring CTR filing
Rs 3 lakh, since even the smallest transaction must be independently reported
Rs 10 lakh, since only exact threshold amounts trigger reporting

explanation.text: The Logic: Under PMLA, every reporting entity must maintain (and report) records of all cash transactions valued at more than Rs 10 lakh in a single transaction, as well as a series of cash transactions individually below Rs 10 lakh that, taken together within a month, aggregate to more than Rs 10 lakh. Here, Rs 3 lakh + Rs 4 lakh + Rs 5 lakh = Rs 12 lakh exceeds the Rs 10 lakh monthly aggregate threshold, so a CTR must be filed with FIU-IND. The Trap: Option A is tempting if candidates focus only on individual transaction size and ignore the monthly aggregation rule. Options C and D misstate the threshold and the qualifying amount. Note: Workbook references: NISM Series XXIV pp.88-89 directly state the monthly aggregate rule for cash-transaction reporting; NISM Series III-A p.173 confirms CTR submission to FIU-IND.
